newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sao Paulo state to use Bovespa's clearing system.
newsitem.headline: Sao Paulo state to use Bovespa's clearing system.

text.p: Sao Paulo state government and Bovespa stock exchange on Wednesday signed an agreement under which the state will use the bolsa's clearing system to consolidate its debt and trade its privatization bonds.
Under the deal, Bovespa will register all Sao Paulo state creditors, advise on the launch of privatization bonds and trade the bonds, said Alfredo Rizkallah, Bovespa's president.

The state government hopes to offer the first tranche of its privatization bonds in April, when it expects to finish consolidating its debt, said Adroaldo Moura e Silva, president of newly created state-owned company CPA.
CPA is in charge of consolidating Sao Paulo's debt and issuing privatization bonds.
Silva said CPA could launch up to 15 billion reais in privatization bonds, which will be backed by Sao Paulo state's firms and other real estate assets.
Under the state's selloff program, investors are allowed to use privatization bonds to pay for at least 30 percent of the price of the state firms, he said.

However, the bonds will not be used at the auction of power utility Companhia Paulista de Forca e Luz (CPFL), scheduled for the second half, because CPFL is not controlled by the state directly, he said.
Sao Paulo state power firm Cesp holds 68.24 percent of CPFL's total capital.
"The bonds can be used in the sale of other power firms such as Cesp and Eletropaulo," he added.
